items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Johnny was aiming for, for Red Nichols.

ctx.x: Was there a particular style you were aiming for in that record, the band?

Johnny was aiming for, for Red Nichols. Uh huh. That's before he, that's before he started imitating Bix. Uh huh. He imitated Nichols. He used to try to play exactly like Nichols. So that's, the arrangements were built around Nichols. That's about, about the time when, when Red was making all those, uh, records with the,
Five pennies and all, yeah. With the pennies.

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: he was doing a lot of recording with Nichols and those guys.

ctx.x: Yeah, Jimmy McPartland was the trumpet player. It was sounding good.

Yeah, Pee-wee, Pee-wee's nose, really, really russling the mind. Is he? Yeah, Pee-wee, when I first went to New York, he was doing a lot of recording with Nichols and those guys. Yeah, yeah. And then the other time, he and Bix were living together.
